How we gather this

Broomfield View doesn't have a newsroom. It collects public information from the sources listed below, checks them twice a day, and shows what they publish: dates, times, places, agenda items, notices and links. We don't write news stories. Some descriptions of places and city projects were written with an AI model from the official pages they cite; we check them against those pages and remove what we cannot back up. No other text on the site is written by an AI model. No person reviews an item before it appears; the checks described below run automatically.

The sources

  • City Council agendas (AgendaLink)
  • National Weather Service forecast
  • National Weather Service alerts
  • CDOT / COtrip
  • Adzuna job listings
  • Glassdoor and Indeed (via aggregated search summaries)
  • Ticketmaster (concerts & tickets)

This list is generated from the same configuration the collectors run from. If a source is switched off, it drops off this page on the next build.

How often

Event calendars, meeting agendas, school and public notices are collected twice a day. Weather is updated every hour. Each page says when it was last updated. A change at the source can take up to half a day to show here; for anything time-critical, use the link to the source.

What we show

  • Meetings: the date, time and place, the agenda item titles exactly as the agenda gives them, and links to the agenda, minutes and video. A meeting is marked Cancelled or Postponed only when the source itself says so in a status or notice field.
  • Events: the title, date, time and venue as the organizer published them, with a link back to the organiser. "Free" and age labels appear only when the source states them.
  • Weather and alerts: forecasts and warnings from the National Weather Service, shown as published.
  • Traffic, school closures and public notices: the notices as the road authority or the school district posts them, with a link.
  • Big shows nearby: concerts, sports and touring shows from Ticketmaster at venues within 25 miles. They are listed separately and are never counted as events in town. Prices are not shown, and distance is measured in a straight line from the town center (shown as "Denver · 13 mi"), not as a driving distance.

What each page is for

Today

It shows: What matters in Broomfield right now: weather alerts, road conditions and events today and tomorrow.

How to use it: Check it before you leave the house or plan the evening. Anything with a warning or closure links to the official notice, which is the one to rely on.

Where it comes from: National Weather Service alerts, local road-condition sources and event organizers' own calendars

Traffic

It shows: Road incidents, lane closures and construction reported near Broomfield, with severity and location.

How to use it: Look before you drive and filter by severity. An empty list means nothing was reported, not that the roads are guaranteed clear. For snow or ice, check the official source too.

Where it comes from: CDOT / COtrip, refreshed with each site update.

Fire and air

It shows: Wildfires within 25 miles of Broomfield and the current air-quality index, each with the source's own numbers and the time it was last updated.

How to use it: Check it when you see smoke or hear about a fire. For a decision about leaving or staying, use the official evacuation pages, not this list.

Where it comes from: Fires: the National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC). Air quality: AirNow, run by the US EPA.

Tonight and this weekend

It shows: Events in Broomfield that start this evening or tomorrow evening, and from Friday evening to Sunday night, grouped by what they are, with the start time and the venue.

How to use it: Pick the group that fits, then open the listing for the source's own details before you go. Times and tickets can change.

Where it comes from: The organizers' own calendars and, where the town has them, Ticketmaster listings and OpenStreetMap opening hours.

What we work out ourselves

Software, not a model, converts times to Broomfield's time zone, removes duplicates between sources, and sorts events into groups from the source's own category or from keywords in the title. Where a source gives no value, we show nothing rather than guess.

What we choose not to name

Meeting agendas sometimes include the names of private individuals — someone applying for a variance, say, or a permit. We show agenda item titles exactly as the agenda gives them, so such a name can appear. We don't collect arrest, jail-booking or obituary sources.

Sources we do not read

If a source's robots.txt forbids automated reading, or it blocks us, we don't collect from it. We show a plain link to it instead, and never try to get around the block.

Photos

Illustrative photos on category and topic pages come from Pexels, each individually credited to its photographer where it appears. They represent the general subject, not a specific event pictured in the story next to them. Ticketmaster images appear on its own listings.

Corrections

If something here is wrong, tell us and we'll fix it — usually within one refresh cycle, since the site rebuilds automatically. Logged corrections are public: see the corrections page.
